# New-ZbxHttpTest

## SYNOPSIS

Creates a web scenario on a host.

## SYNTAX

```
New-ZbxHttpTest [-Name] <string> [-HostReference] <ZabbixReference<ZabbixHost>> [-Step] <ZabbixHttpTestStepRequest[]> [-Delay <string>] [-Retries <int>] [-Agent <string>] [-HttpProxy <string>] [-Status <ZabbixHttpTestStatus>] [-Authentication <ZabbixHttpAuthentication>] [-HttpUser <string>] [-HttpPassword <SecureString>] [-VerifyPeer <bool>] [-VerifyHost <bool>] [-SslCertFile <string>] [-SslKeyFile <string>] [-SslKeyPassword <SecureString>] [-Variable <ZabbixHttpTestVariableRequest[]>] [-Header <ZabbixHttpTestHeaderRequest[]>] [-Tag <ZabbixTagRequest[]>] [-AdditionalProperty <Hashtable>] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

The New-ZbxHttpTest cmdlet creates a web scenario on the host in -Host with httptest.create, then reads it back and writes the ZabbixHttpTest. -Step are the requests in order: objects from New-ZbxHttpTestStep or hashtables keyed by the API's field names; a step without a number is numbered by its position. The server checks the scenario every -Delay and keeps its response codes, times and speeds as items. -WhatIf shows what would be created.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Check that a web shop answers

```powershell
New-ZbxHttpTest -Name 'Web checkout' -Host 'web-01' -Step (New-ZbxHttpTestStep 'Home page' 'https://shop.example.com/' -StatusCodes '200') |
    Select-Object HttpTestId, Name, Delay
```

One step that expects HTTP 200; the scenario runs every minute (the default) on web-01.

### Example 2: Check a login flow every five minutes

```powershell
$steps = @(
    New-ZbxHttpTestStep 'Login page' 'https://shop.example.com/login' -StatusCodes '200'
    New-ZbxHttpTestStep 'Log in' 'https://shop.example.com/login' -Posts @{ name = 'user'; value = 'monitor' }, @{ name = 'password'; value = '{$SHOP.PASSWORD}' } -Required 'Welcome'
)
New-ZbxHttpTest -Name 'Checkout' -Host 'web-01' -Step $steps -Delay '5m' -Tag @{ team = 'shop' } | Select-Object Name, Delay
```

Two steps in order; the second posts a form and expects the text Welcome in the answer.
